observations: At the two 20-percent overviews, the published central main row has a sustained horizontal succession of dark forms; the lower row is weaker. These views locate context, not native stroke detail.

The native known-centre crop resolves a ring-like enclosed pale centre and neighbouring diagonal/vertical/low horizontal forms. The known-left crop retains separated upper clusters and broad lower horizontal/vertical marks. The known-right crop is broad and partly merged. These are already published positive-reference locations, not new letters.

The fixed above-centre crops contain sparse diffuse spots, without a continuous new line I can identify. The below-centre crops have weak bars, crossings and dots, but no defensible new letter sequence from these 1024-square crops alone. The rest of the large image has not been exhaustively inspected at native resolution in this review.

TRACE alone preserves the same main coarse known forms; the claim product darkens/selects their cores and suppresses some weak background. Similarity does not establish model independence, absence of exposure, or a true unknown character.
Blue dashed claim-box borders are present in the author source image and some crops. They are annotation, not ink; the view is a published coloured display, not a raw probability array.
selection_implication: A coherent known positive line with adjacent continuation is a stronger reference context than isolated broad responses on an otherwise uncalibrated unread small crop. It merits designing one controlled continuation test if source/exposure/geometry can be fixed; these five crop positions do not themselves demonstrate unread text.
limits: No new transcription, ink ground truth, or lamina verification.
No model execution and no proof the models are independent.
Above/below crops are not a complete survey of the published area.
